abstract: Four new cases of primary choriocarcinoma arising in the placenta during a seemingly normal gestation were studied at the Trophoblastic Disease Center of Northwestern University. In each case the patient presented with disseminated metastases while carrying an intrauterine gestation with a normally developing fetus. All four placental primaries were small; three of the tumors were microscopic and found only after extensive sectioning. Histologically, these tumors all appeared to arise from the cytotrophoblastic cells covering the stromal portion of villi, and in some areas the involved villi retained a portion of normal investing trophoblast. This study shows that gestational choriocarcinoma unassociated with hydatidiform mole can have an early stage in which chorionic villi are present. The consistently small size of the lesions studied suggests that primary placental choriocarcinoma may frequently be overlooked or missed, and that choriocarcinoma possibly has its origin in the placenta more often than in retained or persistent trophoblast following pregnancy.
abstract_ja: 通常妊娠中に、播種性転移を伴う原発性絨毛癌が胎盤に発生した4例を検討した。全例で正常に発育する胎児とともに子宮内妊娠が継続していた。胎盤原発巣はいずれも小さく、3例は広範な切片作成後にのみ発見された顕微鏡的病変であった。組織学的に、腫瘍は絨毛間質を覆う細胞性栄養膜細胞から生じていた。胞状奇胎を伴わない妊娠性絨毛癌には初期の絨毛が残る段階があることが示された。病変が一貫して小さいことから、胎盤原発の絨毛癌は見逃されやすく、残存・持続性栄養膜由来より胎盤起源の方が多い可能性がある。
